SEASONAL CONTEXT, NOT A CATCH FORECAST

When this trip makes sense.

The official dry-season context is a planning lead, not an exact catch calendar for every target. Ask the captain to explain the intended species and grounds for your week. Rain season, boat operation and fish availability are separate questions.

A reliable month-by-month ranking is not established in this edition. No “best month” score has been invented.

Choose an offshore objective

State whether the goal is a first billfish experience, group participation or a specialist method. Ask how rods are managed and how anglers take turns. A headline fish photograph says little about the experience between strikes. Compare the boat’s facilities, departure point and duration along with the target.

Let the crew own the rigging plan

For a fully equipped charter, ask what personal tackle would actually be useful. Keep rod, reel, line and terminal decisions with the intended technique, rather than importing a reef or inshore setup. Purchase clothing, eye protection and dry storage only after checking what you already have; a charter booking is not a reason to rebuild your entire tackle inventory.

Design a credible alternative

Ask whether a different fishing area or target can be offered if the offshore plan becomes unsuitable. Record what that changes about price and customer expectations. Do not market nearshore roosterfish as the same activity as offshore billfish trolling. Leave room in the travel itinerary for transfers and any agreed weather flexibility.
